title: Sable and the Wreck
premise: When a survey expedition up the Kestrel River goes silent, disgraced mountain guide Silas Dunmore is the only one willing to lead a rescue into territory that got him blacklisted. His small crew — a cartographer's daughter, an ex-constable, and a teenage stowaway — discovers the missing party was murdered to hide illegal mining at the river's forbidden source, and that the concession permits expire in nineteen days, after which the valley will be sealed for a decade. Pursued by the company's private enforcers and betrayed by one of their own, they must document the crime and bring out a surviving witness before the window closes. The book ends with Silas surrendering his own escape to hold the pass, the evidence reaching the capital, and the found family scattering toward uncertain but earned futures.
about_author: Xanthe Nystrom is the pen name of a former river-ranger who spent six seasons mapping headwaters in remote northern concessions before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people the wilderness refuses to forgive.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Silas Dunmore, POV. Broke and blacklisted in the border town of Harrow's Bend, Silas takes a humiliating job hauling freight when word arrives that the Aldervane survey expedition has gone silent on the Kestrel River. He recognizes the route as the one that ended his career. Emotional beat: bitter pride wrestling with the pull of unfinished business.

chapters.title: A Contract in Ash
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The expedition's sponsor, Ilsa Vey of the Cartographic Bureau, offers him double pay and a clean record if he brings back proof of what happened. He signs despite every instinct. Emotional beat: wary hope curdling into the knowledge that no contract ever saved him before.

chapters.title: The Crew
chapters.summary: Maren Oduya, POV. Maren, the cartographer's daughter whose father led the lost expedition, forces her way aboard; ex-constable Bram Hale joins for reasons he won't name. They provision the boat while Silas counts rifles and lies. Emotional beat: strangers sizing each other up, trust not yet earned but needed.

chapters.title: Stowaway
chapters.summary: Tess, POV. A day upriver, the crew discovers fourteen-year-old Tess hidden among the cargo crates, fleeing a workhouse. Silas wants to turn back; Maren argues the current is against them anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility, the first crack in Silas's armor.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Water
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. At the abandoned forward camp they find it ransacked, radios smashed, and a fresh grave marked with a survey stake. Someone else came through recently — and recently means hours. Emotional beat: dread replacing adventure; the mission changes from rescue to reckoning.

chapters.title: Rapids at Dusk
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Running the Sable Narrows at failing light, they lose half their supplies and nearly lose Tess overboard. Maren saves her; Silas says nothing, but starts teaching her knots that night. Emotional beat: survival forging the first real bonds of the found family.

chapters.title: What the Surveyor Left
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. In a waterproof cache, Maren finds her father's field journal: readings that prove the source valley holds ore worth millions, and a final entry saying 'they know we know.' Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose; this is now personal.

chapters.title: The Company Boat
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. A sleek patrol boat flying concession colors shadows them through the fog. Bram recognizes the men aboard as enforcers he once trained before walking away from the constabulary. Emotional beat: old shame resurfacing; Bram confesses part of why he really came.

chapters.title: Portage of Bones
chapters.summary: Tess, POV. Carrying the boat around a waterfall, they find the remains of two survey members, killed execution-style, their instruments destroyed. Tess, who has seen death before, quietly becomes the crew's steadiest hand. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; innocence burned off without breaking.

chapters.title: Turn Back or Go Up
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. With permits expiring in twelve days and enforcers behind them, Silas lays out the brutal math: retreat means the evidence dies with them, advance means the forbidden source. The crew votes to go up. Emotional beat: commitment — each character choosing the hard road for their own reason.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Signal
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram catches someone signaling the patrol boat with a lamp and realizes the leak is Ilsa Vey's own man, Quill, planted in their crew from the start. They confront him; he escapes into the forest with the journal pages proving the ore claim. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deepest because it came from inside.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Rainbound and demoralized, the four share their histories around a wet fire — Silas's disaster on the Vane Glacier, Bram's resignation, Tess's workhouse, Maren's father. Emotional beat: the found family solidifies; they are no longer a crew but a unit.

chapters.title: Quarry Country
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Above the treeline they find the illegal mine: machinery, armed guards, and cages of forced laborers including three survivors of the survey team. One is alive enough to talk — and she saw everything. Emotional beat: horror and fury; the stakes become human lives, not documents.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Tess, POV. Tess, small and invisible, smuggles food to the caged survivor, Odile Ferran, who describes the massacre and where her father hid the original survey plates. Tess promises to come back. Emotional beat: courage without armor; a child keeping faith with a stranger.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Following her father's bearings, they reach the river's forbidden source — a glacial cathedral valley where the plates are cached under a cairn. Enforcers ambush them; Bram is shot covering the retreat. Emotional beat: triumph and cost arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Holding the Pass
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Wounded, Bram insists on staying at the narrow pass with the rifle to buy time, forcing Silas to leave him — the thing Silas failed to do on the Vane Glacier. Emotional beat: redemption through sacrifice; Silas finally does the right thing and hates it.

chapters.title: Descent Under Guns
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Running the rapids downstream at night with Odile and the plates, pursued along both banks, Silas uses every blacklisted trick of his disgrace to stay ahead. Quill reappears on the water and Maren puts him overboard. Emotional beat: the outlaw's skills redeemed in service of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Permit's End
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. They reach the boundary post as the concession expires at dawn, sealing the valley for ten years with Bram still inside. Silas chooses to go back in through the pass rather than abandon him. Emotional beat: the ultimate price of loyalty weighed against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Last Ascent
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas climbs back through the sealed country, finds Bram barely alive, and carries him down the far side on a route only a blacklisted man would know. Emotional beat: grace under exhaustion; the wilderness forgives nothing, but Silas stops asking it to.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. In the capital, Odile's testimony and the plates break the concession scandal open; warrants issue for the company directors. Ilsa Vey tries to bury Silas's role; Odile refuses to let her. Emotional beat: justice achieved through witness, not law alone.

chapters.title: Names Cleared
chapters.summary: Tess, POV. The blacklist is struck; Maren publishes her father's map with all four rescuers credited. Tess, offered a place at the Bureau school, asks instead to apprentice on Silas's next expedition. Emotional beat: the family choosing itself over the institutions that failed them.

chapters.title: Upstream Again
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. A year later, Silas leads a licensed survey up another river with Maren, Bram, and Tess aboard. At the first rapid he looks back once at Harrow's Bend, then faces upstream. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — survival was the price, and it was paid in full.
